details.publicNotes:
Autumnals are melancholy fey that linger in a forest for a single season each year. They arrive just as summer's golden sun begins to gild the first green leaves, and they part after the earth has embraced a forest's last such leaf. Autumnals cull the sick and old so their mulch might fortify vivacious young saplings against winter's privations.

A grove under the care of a "reaping" (between four and ten autumnals, usually) is unmistakable, filled as it is with the mournful dirges the fey sing as they work. A reaping is led by an elder of thirty or forty seasons, who often have access to more advanced primal magic.

Like many forest fey, autumnals are deeply tied to their woodland domains and viciously fight anyone who either preempts or stalls the seasonal cycle of the year. However, one who earns the trust of an autumnal, perhaps by aiding them in purging the woods of unnatural forces, gains more than just a potent ally. They might be gifted with secrets of the forest beyond the ken of even druids or nymphs: the last whispered revelations of ancient oaks, or perhaps the confessions of primordial juggernauts before they finally slipped from this world. These ageless mysteries might have been lost forever had they not been captured and immortalized in the sorrowful songs of the autumnal choir.

Seasonals are a cycle of four kinds of fey, each tied to one of the four seasons: vernals who embody spring's renewal and storming showers, aestivals who embody summer's lazy heat and burning passion, autumnals who embody the melancholy culling and reaping harvest of autumn, and hibernals who embody winter's quiet cheer.

Whatever the current season in the mortal world, seasonals wrap themselves in a metaphysical cloak of their own season's magic and carry the songs full of that season's surging emotions with them wherever they go in the mortal world or across the realm of Faerie. Whenever seasonals meet, shy hibernals typically prefer to amuse themselves by watching the antics of the other three kinds of fey, while vernals impatiently call for energetic contests, aestivals languidly nap until roused to fiery bursts of activity, and autumnals attempt to imbue a sense of stark responsibility in the rest of their compatriots. Exceptions exist, with those seasonals interacting with the others in ways unexpected based upon the stereotypes of their season.

Autumnal Dirges

Autumnals share the history of their forests through their songs: haunting dirges that honor the dying moments of anyone who has drawn their last breath within the autumnals' domain. However, this history is often couched in metaphor that mortals find difficult to parse. Understanding the true meaning of an autumnal dirge might require a successful @Check[Fey Lore|dc:20], @Check[nature|dc:22], or @Check[performance|dc:24] check.

Suggested Monster Parts

Monster Parts 12/27/50 gp

Eligible Refinements weapons (slashing), armor (light, medium), skill items (Acrobatics, Nature, Performance, Stealth)

Eligible Imbued Properties air, bane, charisma, constitution, death, dexterity, energy resistant (vitality, void), music, sensory (low-light vision), spells (Primal: @UUID[Compendium.battlezoo-bestiary-es-pf2e.sf2e-spells.7JgdSTJfI0arGAeF]{Autumn's Howl}, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.g8QqHpv2CWDwmIm1]{Gust of Wind}, @UUID[Compendium.battlezoo-bestiary-es-pf2e.sf2e-spells.oWtpcZ8aq5qQdKri]{Rushing Gust}, @UUID[Compendium.battlezoo-bestiary-es-pf2e.sf2e-spells.PF3gWKYvNgb56kaI]{Songshroud}, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.qvwIwJ9QBihy8R0t]{Speak with Plants}), tangle shield, wild, winged, wisdom, wood

description.value:
You call forth a chill wind that carries with it a barrage of fallen leaves and sharp twigs. All creatures in the area when you call the fallen leaves take 3d6 slashing damage. The winds persist for 1 minute. While the winds last, the area is difficult terrain for creatures both in the air and on the ground. Creatures that end their turn inside the wind take 1d6 persistent piercing damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage from the initial blast increases by 2d6 and the persistent piercing damage for creatures ending their turn inside the wind increases by 1.

You surround yourself in a beautiful melody that echoes in unusual directions, confounding attempts to hear your precise location. While using songshroud, you can't become unnoticed by creatures that can hear. You are @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} to creatures that rely purely on echolocation or other sound-based senses, and you can't become observed by those senses unless they use magic or another special ability and succeed at a counteract check against this spell; as such, you can use songshroud in combination with becoming @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} (or foiling vision in a different way) to avoid being observed by a creature with both vision and echolocation. The shroud also protects you from harmful sounds, granting you a +1 status bonus to saving throws against auditory effects and resistance 5 to sonic damage. When you speak, you can choose to either project your voice normally or to use the song to hide it. If you choose to hide it, creatures that are farther than 5 feet away must succeed at a Perception check against your spell DC to overhear what you are saying.

@UUID[Compendium.battlezoo-bestiary-es-pf2e.sf2e-effects.Item.h0eng2GtJpOuRndn]{Spell Effect: Songshroud}

Heightened (4th) The resistance to sonic damage increases to 10, the duration increases to 10 minutes, and the status bonus on saving throws against auditory effects increases to +2.

Heightened (7th) The resistance to sonic damage increases to 15, the duration increases to 10 minutes, and the status bonus on saving throws against auditory effects increases to +3.

A violent wind issues forth from your palm, blowing from the point where you are when you Cast the Spell to the line's opposite end. The wind extinguishes small non-magical fires, disperses fog and mist, blows objects of light Bulk or less around, and pushes larger objects. Large or smaller creatures in the area must attempt a Fortitude save. Large or smaller creatures that later move into the gust must attempt the save on entering.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature can't move against the wind.

Failure The creature is knocked @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. If it was flying, it takes the effects of critical failure instead.

Critical Failure The creature is pushed 30 feet in the wind's direction, knocked prone, and takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage.

duration.value: until the start of your next turn

description.value:
You stir up the air around you to propel yourself toward a foe, then slice into them with blades of air. Stride up to half your Speed toward a target, then make a melee spell attack roll against the target's AC. If you hit, the target takes 2d4 slashing damage (double damage on a critical hit).

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d4.

You can ask questions of and receive answers from plants and fungi, but the spell doesn't make them more friendly or intelligent than normal. Most normal plants and fungi have a distinctive view of the world around them, so they don't recognize details about creatures or know anything about the world beyond their immediate vicinity. Cunning plant or fungus monsters are likely to be terse and evasive, while less intelligent ones often make inane comments.

Heightened (4th) The duration is 8 hours.

Trigger A living creature within 30 feet dies

Requirements The dying creature is level 2 or higher

Effect The autumnal is strengthened by the fleeting life essence, gaining 5 temporary Hit Points that last for 1 minute.

@UUID[Compendium.battlezoo-bestiary-es-pf2e.sf2e-effects.Item.vfQXTmtrzj1LxmIl]{Effect: Life from Death}
Leaves swirl about the autumnal whenever they use a move action to move at least 5 feet, granting them concealment until the end of their current turn.
The autumnal Strides or Flies twice, making a leaf blade Strike against a creature at any time during the movement.

The autumnal singles out a creature within 60 feet for reaping. A mark of a scythe appears on the creature's body, which must then roll a @Check[fortitude|dc:20] save to determine the mark's duration. While the mark lasts, any autumnal who Strikes the marked creature does an additional 1d4 precision damage. This damage is void if the marked creature is living, or vitality if they are undead. In addition, if the marked creature is living, it must roll twice and take the lower result on any recovery checks to reduce its dying condition. The mark disappears automatically if the autumnal uses Mark for Reaping on another creature or if the autumnal dies.

Critical Success The mark disappears immediately.

Success The mark lasts for 1 round.

Failure The mark lasts for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The mark lasts for 10 minutes.
